newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks rise early, blue chips gain.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks rise early, blue chips gain.

text.p: Singapore shares rose early on Tuesday, propelled by institutional demand for blue chip stocks and expectations of improved second-half company earnings.
"Everyone's been expecting a turnaround early this year and are beginning to adjust their positions," a dealer with a foreign securities company said.
He said the market focus was on electronics and technology stocks, although institutions encouraged by the strong Dow Jones overnight were also nibbling at blue chip stocks.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose 14.11 points to 2,259.83 at 0200 GMT, on a moderate volume of 42 million lots.
SIA Foreign gained early to Singapore $13.40, up $0.30, on a newspaper report that the airline was considering floating its subsidiaries.
A company official was quoted as saying by the Business Times that SIA's cargo division might be spun off as an independent unit within the next two to three years.
Other gainers included SPH Foreign at S$29.00, up $0.60, but dealers cited merely index-linked demand.
Among actives were multimedia company Aztech at S$0.58, up $0.02, and electronic firm Eltech at S$0.44, up $0.015.
